newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Anadolu Sigorta plans 90 pct rise in premiums.
newsitem.headline: Turk Anadolu Sigorta plans 90 pct rise in premiums.

text.p: Turkey's leading insurer Anadolu Anonim Turk Sigorta Sirketi aims to raise its total premium revenue by 90 percent in 1997, over more than nine trillion lira expected for 1996, a senior company official said.
"We estimate Turkey's 1997 inflation will stand at 80 percent and target to increase our premiums by 90 percent," Ahmet Yavuz, general manager of the company, told Reuters.
"So our aim is to grow 10 percent in real terms in 1997," he added.
The shares of the company are traded on the Istanbul stock market. They stood at 5,500 lira at midday on Monday, compared to 5,700 at Friday's close.
The company was the leader of the Turkish insurance sector, with premiums totalling 5.02 trillion lira in 1995, 9.4 percent of the country total.
Yavuz said the expected 1996 results would show growth of 85-90 percent in premiums and the company would keep its leadership.
"We started a new automation project to boost our premiums to meet the 1997 targets," he said.

The project aims to build a network between agencies and the company which will enable the agencies to produce 60 different types of insurance policies on a real-time/on-line basis, the first such practice in Turkey's insurance sector.
Anadolu Sigorta aims to raise the number of agencies connected to the network to 125 this year from current 60 and to raise about 40 percent of total premiums through them.
The main shareholder of the company is Turkiye Is Bankasi, Turkey's biggest private bank with a 54.89 percent stake.

"We have a four-year target to connect all our agencies to the network...We also plan to train Is Bank's 815 branches to be able to directly produce insurance policies in the future, starting with the biggest 30 branches this year," Yavuz said.
Anadolu Sigorta reported an 86.1 percent growth in premiums to 5.95 trillion lira in the first nine months of 1996 over 3.20 trillion lira in the same 1995 period.
Its net profits surged 188.8 percent in the first nine months of 1996 to 1.16 trillion lira against 402.7 billion lira in the same period of 1995.
Yavuz said a 169.8 percent jump in financial income, led by interest earnings from government securities was the main reason behind the sharp profit increase.
